questions.stem: A team wants to query Lambda logs by fields such as requestId, userId and orderStatus in CloudWatch Logs Insights. How should the functions write their logs?

options.text: As free-form text sentences that mention each field's value
options.rationale: Free text needs fragile parsing in every query.

options.text: As print statements with no named fields
options.rationale: Unstructured output cannot be filtered by field.

options.text: As structured JSON, with those fields as keys
options.rationale: Logs Insights discovers JSON fields so queries can filter and group on them.

options.text: To a local file in /tmp
options.rationale: Files in /tmp are lost when the environment is recycled and are not in CloudWatch Logs.

questions.explanation: Structured logging makes logs searchable and easy to turn into metrics.

questions.stem: A Lambda function must publish a custom business metric on every invocation, without adding a synchronous CloudWatch API call to each request. What should the developer use?

options.text: A PutMetricData API call from the handler on every invocation
options.rationale: This adds a synchronous API call to each request.

options.text: X-Ray annotations on each trace
options.rationale: Annotations index traces; they are not CloudWatch metrics.

options.text: An Amazon SNS message for each value
options.rationale: SNS delivers messages; it does not create metrics.

options.text: Embedded metric format (EMF) in the function's log output
options.rationale: CloudWatch extracts the metric from the structured log event asynchronously.

questions.explanation: EMF lets code emit metrics through logs, with no extra API call.

questions.stem: An application on Amazon EC2 instances must publish a custom metric for the number of items in an in-memory queue. Which approaches will publish it to CloudWatch? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Enable EC2 detailed monitoring
options.rationale: Detailed monitoring adds one-minute EC2 metrics, not application values.

options.text: Send the value to the CloudWatch agent, for example through StatsD
options.rationale: The agent collects custom metrics and publishes them to CloudWatch.

options.text: Change the X-Ray sampling rate
options.rationale: Sampling controls tracing, not metrics.

options.text: Call the PutMetricData API from the application through the AWS SDK
options.rationale: PutMetricData publishes custom metric data points.

options.text: Turn on AWS CloudTrail data events
options.rationale: CloudTrail records API activity, not application values.

questions.explanation: Custom metrics come from PutMetricData, the CloudWatch agent or embedded metric format logs.

questions.stem: The team wants an email when a function's error count goes above 10 in five minutes. What should the developer set up?

options.text: A CloudWatch alarm on the Errors metric that notifies an SNS topic
options.rationale: The alarm changes state at the threshold and notifies the topic's email subscribers.

options.text: An X-Ray group with a filter expression for requests that have errors
options.rationale: Groups organize traces; they do not send email.

options.text: A CloudWatch Logs retention policy
options.rationale: Retention controls log storage.

options.text: An X-Ray sampling rule for failed requests
options.rationale: Sampling rules decide which requests are traced; they do not send notifications.

questions.explanation: Alarms watch metrics and notify through SNS.

questions.stem: Developers want an email each time an AWS CodePipeline execution succeeds or fails. What should the developer configure?

options.text: A CloudWatch Logs metric filter on the CodeBuild logs that counts failed builds
options.rationale: Build logs do not carry the pipeline's overall result in a reliable way.

options.text: An EventBridge rule for pipeline state changes that targets an SNS topic
options.rationale: CodePipeline emits state-change events that rules can route to notifications.

options.text: A manual approval action at the end of the pipeline
options.rationale: Approvals pause the pipeline; they do not notify on completion.

options.text: AWS CloudTrail Insights
options.rationale: CloudTrail Insights detects unusual API activity.

questions.explanation: Deployment and pipeline events flow through EventBridge, which can notify on completion.

questions.stem: A team wants to be warned before its Lambda functions reach the account's concurrency limit. What should a CloudWatch alarm watch?

options.text: The average Duration metric of the busiest function, measured over five minutes
options.rationale: Duration measures run time, not concurrency.

options.text: The Invocations metric of one function
options.rationale: Invocations count requests, not concurrent instances.

options.text: ClaimedAccountConcurrency compared with the account's concurrency quota
options.rationale: Lambda uses this metric to track how much account concurrency is already claimed, including reserved and provisioned concurrency.

options.text: The number of Lambda Invoke events recorded by CloudTrail
options.rationale: CloudTrail events are API records, not a concurrency measure.

questions.explanation: Lambda's documentation recommends alarming on ClaimedAccountConcurrency against the quota; ConcurrentExecutions alone can understate what is claimed.

questions.stem: A developer wants to search X-Ray traces by customer ID to investigate one customer's slow requests. How should the code record the customer ID?

options.text: As metadata on the segment
options.rationale: Metadata is stored with the trace but is not indexed for search.

options.text: As a CloudWatch metric dimension
options.rationale: Metric dimensions do not make traces searchable.

options.text: In the function's environment variables
options.rationale: Environment variables are configuration, not per-request data.

options.text: As an annotation on the segment
options.rationale: Annotations are indexed, so filter expressions can search on them.

questions.explanation: Use annotations for values you filter on and metadata for extra detail.

questions.stem: A developer wants end-to-end traces for requests that go through an API Gateway REST API, a Lambda function and DynamoDB. Which steps are needed? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Turn on CloudTrail data events for the table
options.rationale: CloudTrail records API calls for auditing, not traces.

options.text: Enable detailed monitoring on the API
options.rationale: Detailed metrics do not connect a request's path across services.

options.text: Turn on active tracing for the Lambda function and instrument its AWS SDK calls
options.rationale: Lambda records its segment, and instrumentation records the DynamoDB calls.

options.text: Enable VPC Flow Logs
options.rationale: Flow logs record network traffic metadata, not request traces.

options.text: Enable X-Ray tracing on the API Gateway stage
options.rationale: API Gateway then starts or continues the trace for each request.

questions.explanation: Tracing must be on at each hop, plus SDK instrumentation for downstream calls.

questions.stem: An Application Load Balancer keeps routing requests to instances whose application has stopped responding. The health check uses the default path /, which the web server still answers. What should the developer change?

options.text: Point the target group's health check at an application path such as /health
options.rationale: The load balancer stops routing to targets that fail the check.

options.text: Increase the load balancer's idle timeout so that slow targets have more time to answer
options.rationale: Idle timeout affects connection reuse, not health.

options.text: Turn on access logs
options.rationale: Access logs record requests; they do not take targets out of service.

options.text: Add a second listener on port 443
options.rationale: Another listener does not detect unhealthy targets.

questions.explanation: Health checks should exercise the application, not just the port.

questions.stem: On Amazon EKS, new pods receive traffic before they finish loading their cache, and early requests fail. What should the developer add to the pod specification?

options.text: A liveness probe that restarts the pod when the cache is missing
options.rationale: Liveness probes restart containers; restarts would not stop early traffic.

options.text: A readiness probe that succeeds once the cache is loaded
options.rationale: Pods receive traffic only once their readiness probe succeeds.

options.text: A larger memory limit
options.rationale: More memory does not delay traffic until the pod is ready.

options.text: An extra replica of the deployment
options.rationale: More pods still receive traffic too early.

questions.explanation: Readiness controls traffic; liveness controls restarts.
